newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia palm oil output seen up, prices down.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil output seen up, prices down.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil production was expected to rise two percent to 8.2 million tonnes in 1997 from the 8.04 million tonnes forecast this year, the Finance Ministry said in its annual economic report.

The average price of palm oil was expected to fall 7.1 percent to 1,100 ringgit a tonne in 1997 from the 1,184.50 ringgit forecast in 1996, the report said. Current palm oil prices are quoting at around 1,155 ringgit.
Export volumes, however, were expected to rise as world stocks of vegetable oils, in particular soybeans, was forecast to decline 15.76 percent in 1995/96, the report said.
"Considering that palm oil is one of the world's most efficiently produced vegetable oils, it would be able to continue to take advantage of this shortfall," it said.
The lower price of palm oil, compared to other vegetable oils and fats, has also boosted demand for the Malaysian commodity, it said.

Imports from price-sensitive countries such as Pakistan, India, Egypt and South America have been particularly encouraging, the report said. Leading importers for the first half of this year were Pakistan, China and India, with a combined offtake of 1.33 million tonnes.
